plainLanguage: Section 22 inaeleza nani anaweza kuhesabiwa principal offender. Si mtu aliyefanya physical act pekee: anayesaidia kuwezesha, anayeaid/abet, na anayecounsel au procure mwingine anaweza pia deemed to have taken part and be guilty of the offence.
meaning: Subsection (1) ina categories nne za participation. Paragraph (a) ni actual perpetrator; (b) ni act/omission done for purpose of enabling or aiding; (c) ni aiding/abetting; (d) ni counselling/procuring. Subsections (2)-(3) zinaweka charging na consequences za counselling/procuring. Subsection (4) pia inashughulikia procuring another to perform an act/omission ambayo ingekuwa offence kama procurer mwenyewe angeifanya.
keyPoints: Actual perpetrator ni principal offender under (1)(a).
Enabling/aiding conduct under (1)(b) inaweza kuleta principal liability.
Aiding or abetting under (1)(c) ni separate statutory route.
Counsellor/procurer may be charged as committing or counselling/procuring under subsection (2).
Conviction for counselling/procuring has same consequences as conviction of committing under subsection (3).
Subsection (4) covers procurement of another's act/omission where the procurer's own performance would constitute an offence.

legalTerms.meaning: Mtu ambaye section 22 inamdeem kuwa ameshiriki na kuwa guilty of the offence.
Kutoa msaada unaohusiana na commission ya offence.
Kuhamasisha/kusaidia commission ya offence katika sense ya criminal participation.
Kushauri au kuhimiza mwingine kufanya offence.
Kusababisha/kufanikisha mwingine kufanya act au offence kwa namna inayotambuliwa na section 22.

examples.title: Dereva anayesaidia robbery
examples.scenario: A anajua mpango wa robbery na kwa purpose ya kuwezesha offence anawaendesha offenders kwenda na kutoka eneo la tukio.
examples.analysis: Depending on proof of purpose and participation, facts zinaweza kuchunguzwa chini ya section 22(1)(b) au (c); kuwa nje ya building hakumalizi liability.

examples.title: Mtu anayeshauri offence
examples.scenario: A anamshawishi B kufanya offence na B anaifanya.
examples.analysis: Section 22(1)(d), (2) na (3) zinaweza kufanya counselling/procuring route kuwa legally equivalent in consequences to committing the offence.

cases.name: Augustino Mwenda v Republic
cases.relevance: Tanzanian appellate authority discussing principal-offender liability and the need for evidence connecting an accused to participation rather than guilt by association.

history.summary: Section 22 begins Chapter V, Parties to Offences, and codifies multiple forms of participation as principal liability rather than limiting guilt to the hand that physically completes the offence.
notes: During this digitisation pass, repository section 22 was found truncated after subsection (1). Subsections (2)-(4) were restored from the official R.E. 2022 text.
Sections 22, 23 and 24 should be distinguished: participation, common intention/common purpose, and consequences of counselling are related but separate rules.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo A
expertPerspectives.view: Identify the accused's own act or omission first and map it to paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d); presence or association alone should not substitute for evidence of participation.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo B
expertPerspectives.view: For enabling/aiding allegations, the purpose and context of the accused's conduct can distinguish innocent assistance from criminal participation.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo C
expertPerspectives.view: Section 22 deliberately removes the assumption that only the person who physically completes the offence can be treated as a principal offender.

debateQuestion: Ni act, omission, aid, abetment, counsel au procurement gani inayomhusisha accused, na evidence inaunganisha conduct hiyo na commission ya offence kwa kiwango gani?
disclaimer: Ufafanuzi huu si maandishi rasmi ya sheria.
